definition: Euphemistic slang for the clitoris, comparing the glans clitoridis to a pearl in shape and smoothness.
notes: 'Pearl' as a clitoral metaphor also appears sporadically in English erotica, but is far more entrenched in Spanish usage.

definition: The most widespread Spanish slang term for the clitoris, derived from 'button' and describing its shape and prominence at the top of the vulva.
notes: 'Button' is also used in English as a clitoral euphemism, making this a near-parallel metaphor across both languages.

definition: Slang for the clitoris derived from 'pip' or 'seed', emphasizing its small size; common in Latin American Spanish.
notes: More prevalent in Latin American varieties than in Iberian Spanish; the seed/pip metaphor highlights smallness rather than function.

definition: Euphemistic slang for the clitoris, derived from 'little bell', evoking its pendant shape when the hood is retracted.
notes: Also the Spanish name for the fairy Tinker Bell (Campanita de Peter Pan), which lends a playful register; less common than botón or pepita.

definition: Diminutive affectionate euphemism for the clitoris, a softened variant of perla ('little pearl') emphasizing smallness and delicacy.
notes: The -ita diminutive adds tenderness or erotic diminution; slightly lower recognition than the base form perla.

definition: The standard informal-to-neutral Spanish word for buttocks; used freely in everyday speech, sexual contexts, and public health materials.
notes: More anatomically grounded than trasero; functions as the unmarked default in most Latin American dialects; slightly more clinical-feeling in Spain.

definition: Common euphemism for the buttocks derived from 'rear/back part'; the most socially neutral and widely acceptable term in polite Spanish conversation.
notes: Functionally parallel to English 'rear end' or 'backside'; safe for use in mixed-age company and broadcast media.

definition: Mexican and Central American slang for the buttocks; informal and widely used within its regional range.
notes: Recognition drops sharply outside Mexico and Central America; largely opaque to speakers in Spain or South America's Southern Cone.

definition: Literary and somewhat dated term for the buttocks, etymologically linked to 'posar' (to sit/rest), indicating the part of the body one sits upon.
notes: More common in literary prose and older journalism than in contemporary informal speech; recognition declines among speakers under 40.

definition: Informal term for the buttocks or haunches transferred from animal anatomy, used figuratively for the human posterior.
notes: Primary meaning is animal hindquarters; human application is informal and regional; recognition lower among urban and younger speakers.

definition: Childish or playful diminutive for the buttocks, typically used by or for children or in affectionate intimate adult speech.
notes: Near-zero crude score in most contexts; rarely used in explicitly sexual discourse; functions more like English 'bum' or 'tush' in register.

definition: Diminutive of 'culo' (ass), used to describe a small or attractive buttocks; common in sexual compliments and erotica.
notes: The -ito diminutive softens the base vulgarity of culo while adding an erotic or affectionate charge; standard fare in reggaeton lyrics and digital sexual communication.

definition: Augmentative of 'culo' (ass), meaning a notably large and impressive buttocks; used almost exclusively in admiring sexual contexts.
notes: The -azo augmentative suffix signals either large size or forceful impact; in this case emphatic admiration; analogous to English 'phat ass' in connotation.

definition: Argentine and Rioplatense slang for the buttocks or lower back region, transferred from the culinary term for an animal's loin cut.
notes: Primary meaning is a cut of meat (pork loin); the anatomical transfer is mainly Argentine; sexual meaning is context-dependent and not reliably parsed outside that dialect zone.

definition: Clinical term for coitus, specifically penile-vaginal sexual intercourse; the standard medical term for heterosexual penetrative sex.
notes: Direct cognate of Latin coitus; used in medical, legal, and sex-education registers; lower frequency in everyday informal speech than relaciones sexuales.

definition: Highly clinical and formal term for sexual intercourse or copulation; used in scientific, legal, and literary contexts.
notes: Also carries the grammatical meaning of copula (linking verb) in Spanish linguistics, which can cause register ambiguity; more elevated in tone than coito.

definition: The universally understood neutral phrase for sexual intercourse or sexual activity in Spanish; the default in sex education, public health, and journalism.
notes: Phrase-level entry; the go-to neutral formulation across all Spanish-speaking countries and the term taught in school sex education curricula.

definition: Clinical term for sexual penetration; the insertion of a penis, finger, or object into a bodily orifice.
notes: Direct cognate with English 'penetration'; appears in clinical, legal, and erotic registers; higher crude score than most clinical terms because it is also common in pornographic description.

definition: Clinical term for fellatio; oral stimulation of the penis.
notes: Direct Spanish adaptation of Latin/English fellatio; used in medical, legal, and sex-education contexts; the slang term mamada vastly outnumbers felación in informal speech.

definition: Latin-derived clinical term for oral stimulation of the vulva or vagina; a direct loanword retained identically from Latin in both Spanish and English medical vocabulary.
notes: Orthographically and phonetically identical in Spanish and English; used in clinical and formal sexual-health contexts; colloquial equivalents (lamer, comer el coño) dominate informal speech.

definition: Clinical term for masturbation; self-stimulation of the genitals for sexual pleasure or orgasm.
notes: Near-identical cognate with English 'masturbation'; the standard term across sex education, public health, and clinical settings throughout the Spanish-speaking world.

definition: Legal and religious term for sodomy; historically encompassing anal intercourse, oral sex, and other non-procreative sexual acts; derived from the biblical city of Sodom.
notes: Moral loading is heavier in Spanish than in contemporary English due to the stronger historical influence of the Catholic Church; still appears in legal codes of several Latin American countries.

definition: Clinical phrase for anal intercourse; the medical and legal standard for penetrative anal sex.
notes: Two-word clinical phrase used primarily in medical, legal, and epidemiological discourse; sexo anal is more common in informal health communication and everyday speech.

definition: Clinical phrase for oral sex, encompassing both fellatio and cunnilingus.
notes: Somewhat stilted even in clinical usage; sexo oral is far more common in public health materials and everyday speech; coito oral is more strictly formal or legal in register.

definition: Clinical term for ejaculation; the expulsion of semen from the penis at orgasm.
notes: Near-identical cognate with English 'ejaculation'; understood across clinical, educational, and lay registers; also used in phrases like eyaculación precoz (premature ejaculation).
